claim: After you apply an AWS Backup continuous backup rule to an RDS instance, you cannot create or modify continuous backup settings in Amazon RDS; you make changes through the AWS Backup console or CLI.
question: Where can you change continuous backup settings of an RDS instance covered by an AWS Backup continuous rule?

values.display: can't create or modify continuous backup settings in Amazon RDS
through the AWS Backup console or the AWS Backup CLI

qualifiers.scope: RDS instances with AWS Backup continuous backups

evidence.quote: After you apply an AWS Backup continuous backup rule to an Amazon RDS instance, you can't create or modify continuous backup settings in Amazon RDS. You must make modifications through the AWS Backup console or the AWS Backup CLI.

claim: You cannot create copies of RDS continuous backups because AWS Backup for RDS does not allow copying transaction logs; instead AWS Backup creates a snapshot and copies it with the frequency set in the backup plan.
question: Can an RDS continuous backup be copied to another Region?

values.display: can't create copies of Amazon RDS continuous backups
does not allow copying transaction logs

evidence.quote: You can't create copies of Amazon RDS continuous backups because AWS Backup for Amazon RDS does not allow copying transaction logs. Instead, AWS Backup creates a snapshot and copies it with the frequency specified in the backup plan.

claim: You can perform a point-in-time restore of an RDS instance using either AWS Backup or Amazon RDS.
question: Can you do the point-in-time restore of an RDS instance in the RDS service when AWS Backup manages the continuous backup?

values.display: using either AWS Backup or Amazon RDS
point-in-time restore

evidence.quote: You can perform a point-in-time restore using either AWS Backup or Amazon RDS.

claim: Aurora continuous backups are supported in vaults protected by Vault Lock, with the vault's retention settings enforced, but they do not support the logically air-gapped vault feature; to use a logically air-gapped vault with Aurora, use periodic snapshot backups.
question: Can an Aurora continuous backup be stored in a logically air-gapped vault?

values.display: do not support the logically air-gapped vault feature
use periodic snapshot backups instead

evidence.quote: Aurora continuous backups are supported in vaults protected by AWS Backup Vault Lock, and the vault's minimum and maximum retention settings are enforced on the recovery point. However, Aurora continuous backups do not support the logically air-gapped vault feature. To use a logically air-gapped vault with Aurora, use periodic snapshot backups instead.

claim: The recovery point objective (RPO) for Aurora continuous backups is typically less than 5 minutes, because Aurora copies data to Amazon S3 continuously in the background.
question: What RPO do Aurora continuous backups give?

values.display: typically less than 5 minutes
copies data to Amazon S3 continuously

evidence.quote: The recovery point objective (RPO) for Aurora continuous backups is typically less than 5 minutes, as Aurora copies data to Amazon S3 continuously in the background.

claim: If a continuous backup rule also specifies a cross-account or cross-Region copy, AWS Backup takes a snapshot of the resource and copies the snapshot to the destination vault, and AWS Backup does not support on-demand copies of continuous backups.
question: How is a continuous backup copied to another Region or account?

values.display: takes a snapshot of the resource and copies the snapshot
does not support on-demand copies of continuous backups

evidence.quote: If a continuous backup rule also specifies a cross-account or cross-Region copy and AWS Backup supports the operation for the resource type, AWS Backup takes a snapshot of the resource and copies the snapshot to the destination vault.
AWS Backup does not support on-demand copies of continuous backups.

claim: Every backup after the first full one is incremental, but all AWS Backup backups keep the reference data needed for a full restore, even after the original full backup has reached the end of its lifecycle and been deleted.
question: Can you still do a full restore from an incremental backup after the first full backup was deleted?

values.display: retain the necessary reference data to allow a full restore
even if the original (full) backup has reached the end of its lifecycle

evidence.quote: Although each backup after the first (full) one is incremental (meaning it only captures changes from the previous backup), all backups made with AWS Backup retain the necessary reference data to allow a full restore. This is true even if the original (full) backup has reached the end of its lifecycle and been deleted.

claim: A backup of a fully managed resource can be incremental only if its vault also contains an earlier backup; other resource types can have incremental backups as long as there is a previous backup of the resource in the same Region.
question: When can a backup of a fully managed resource be incremental?

values.display: only be incremental if the vault in which the backup is created also contains an earlier backup
within the same Region

evidence.quote: Backups of resources which are fully managed by AWS Backup can only be incremental if the vault in which the backup is created also contains an earlier backup (incremental or full); other resource types (not fully managed by AWS Backup) can have incremental backups as long as there is a previous backup of the resource within the same Region.

claim: Some resources, such as Aurora, offer incremental backup only through continuous backups and point-in-time restore, not through snapshot-based backups.
question: Does Aurora get incremental backups from AWS Backup snapshot rules?

values.display: only through continuous backups and point-in-time restore (PITR)
not through snapshot-based backups

evidence.quote: Some resources, such as Amazon Aurora, offer incremental backup only through continuous backups and point-in-time restore (PITR), not through snapshot-based backups.

claim: To back up an EC2 instance, the instance can be running or stopped but not terminated, because only a running or stopped instance can communicate with AWS Backup.
question: Can AWS Backup back up a stopped EC2 instance?

values.display: can be in the running or stopped state
but not the terminated state

evidence.quote: To back up an Amazon EC2 instance, the instance can be in the `running` or `stopped` state, but not the `terminated` state. This is because a `running` or `stopped` instance can communicate with AWS Backup, but a `terminated` instance cannot.

claim: AWS Backup retains previously created backups consistent with your lifecycle policy, regardless of the health of the source resource.
question: Are backups kept if the source resource becomes unhealthy or is deleted?

values.display: regardless of the health of your source resource
consistent with your lifecycle policy

evidence.quote: AWS Backup retains previously-created backups consistent with your lifecycle policy, regardless of the health of your source resource.

claim: Copies keep their source configuration, including the creation date (the time the source was created, not the copy) and the retention period, though you can override the retention period.
question: Which creation date and retention does a backup copy keep?

values.display: Copies retain their source configuration
You can override the retention period

evidence.quote: Copies retain their source configuration, including creation dates and retention period. The creation date refers to when the source was created, not when the copy was created. You can override the retention period.

claim: Backups in cold storage or archive tiers cannot be copied across accounts or Regions.
question: Can a backup that is in cold storage be copied to another Region or account?

values.display: backups in cold storage or archive tiers cannot be copied
most resource types

evidence.quote: You can copy backups to multiple AWS accounts or AWS Regions on demand or automatically as part of a scheduled backup plan for most resource types, though backups in cold storage or archive tiers cannot be copied.

claim: AWS Backup does not provide any service-level agreements (SLAs) for copy job completion times; copy times vary with system load, capacity and resource size.
question: Does AWS Backup guarantee a completion time for copy jobs?

values.display: does not provide any service-level agreements (SLAs)
copy job completion times

evidence.quote: AWS Backup does not provide any service-level agreements (SLAs) for copy job completion times. Copy times can vary based upon system load, capacity, and the size of the resources being copied, even for copy jobs containing the same resources.

claim: Only one backup or copy job can run at a time for a given resource; additional copy jobs for that resource stay in CREATED status until the running job completes.
question: How many backup or copy jobs can run at once for one resource?

values.display: Only one backup or copy job can run at a time
remain in CREATED status

evidence.quote: Only one backup or copy job can run at a time for a given resource. Additional copy jobs for the same resource remain in `CREATED` status until the running job completes.

claim: Recovery points that AWS Backup could not delete (status EXPIRED) stay in your account and might increase your storage costs until you delete them manually.
question: What happens to recovery points that AWS Backup could not delete?

values.display: continue to store expired recovery points in your account
increase your storage costs

evidence.quote: You will continue to store expired recovery points in your account. This might increase your storage costs.

claim: Updating a backup plan affects the recovery points it creates in the future, but not the recovery points it has already created.
question: Does editing a backup plan change the retention of existing recovery points?

values.display: affects the future recovery points it will create
does not affect the recovery point it already created

evidence.quote: Updating the backup plan affects the future recovery points it will create, but does not affect the recovery point it already created.
